# Data Preparation

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

efcu <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")
```

## Dataset Overview

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dataset
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of the Case 31 Dataset"

data.frame(
  Description = c("Number of Observations", 
                  "Number of Variables"),
  Value = c(nrow(efcu), ncol(efcu))
) |>
  kable()
```

# R3: Attitudes Toward Credit Union Employees

This research question examines members' attitudes toward credit union employees using survey items Q3 through Q6.

## Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
#| include: false

r3_vars <- c("q3", "q4", "q5", "q6")

lapply(r3_vars, function(v) {
  list(
    Question = v,
    Description = attr(efcu[[v]], "label"),
    Labels = attr(efcu[[v]], "labels"),
    Frequency = table(efcu[[v]], useNA = "ifany")
  )
})
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-descriptive
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive Statistics for Attitudes Toward Credit Union Employees"

r3_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r3_vars, function(v) {
  x <- as.numeric(efcu[[v]])
  x <- x[x %in% 1:5]

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(v),
    N = length(x),
    Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
    SD = round(sd(x), 3),
    Minimum = min(x),
    Maximum = max(x)
  )
}))

kable(r3_summary)
```

## One-Sample t-test

A one-sample t-test was conducted for each survey item to determine whether members' attitudes toward credit union employees differed significantly from the neutral midpoint of 3.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-ttest
#| tbl-cap: "One-Sample t-test Results for R3"

r3_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r3_vars, function(v) {
  x <- as.numeric(efcu[[v]])
  x <- x[x %in% 1:5]

  test <- t.test(x, mu = 3)

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(v),
    N = length(x),
    Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
    SD = round(sd(x), 3),
    t = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 3),
    df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
    P_Value = format.pval(test$p.value,
                         digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    Significant = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05,
                         "Yes", "No")
  )
}))

kable(r3_tests)
```

## Data Visualization

```{r}
#| label: fig-r3-ratings
#| fig-cap: "Mean Ratings of Attitudes Toward Credit Union Employees"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(r3_summary, aes(x = Question, y = Mean)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 3,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Mean)),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 5),
    breaks = 0:5
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Survey Question",
    y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Findings and Insights

Members generally have positive attitudes toward credit union
employees. The mean ratings for Q3 through Q6 range from
4.078 to 4.352, indicating favorable perceptions of employee
proficiencies.

All four mean ratings are significantly higher than the neutral
midpoint of 3 (p < .001). Q3 received the highest mean rating
(M = 4.352), followed by Q4 (M = 4.312). Q5 and Q6 received
slightly lower but still positive ratings (M = 4.078).

These findings suggest that employee proficiency is a strength
of the credit union, although there is still room for improvement
in the areas represented by Q5 and Q6.

## Composite Scale: Employee Proficiency

Based on the previous reliability and factor analyses,
Q3 through Q6 were combined into a composite measure
named Att_Employee.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-composite
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive Statistics for Employee Proficiency"

efcu$Att_Employee <- rowMeans(
  efcu[, c("q3", "q4", "q5", "q6")],
  na.rm = FALSE
)

x <- na.omit(efcu$Att_Employee)

data.frame(
  Variable = "Att_Employee",
  N = length(x),
  Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
  SD = round(sd(x), 3),
  Minimum = min(x),
  Maximum = max(x)
) |>
  kable()
```

## One-Sample t-test for Employee Proficiency

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-composite-test
#| tbl-cap: "One-Sample t-test for Employee Proficiency"

employee_test <- t.test(
  efcu$Att_Employee,
  mu = 3
)

data.frame(
  Variable = "Att_Employee",
  Mean = round(mean(efcu$Att_Employee, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
  t = round(as.numeric(employee_test$statistic), 3),
  df = as.numeric(employee_test$parameter),
  P_Value = format.pval(employee_test$p.value,
                        digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
  Lower_CI = round(employee_test$conf.int[1], 3),
  Upper_CI = round(employee_test$conf.int[2], 3)
) |>
  kable()
```

The composite scale for employee proficiency has a mean
of 4.205 (SD = 0.594). The one-sample t-test indicates
that the mean is significantly higher than the neutral
midpoint of 3, t(127) = 22.954, p < .001,
95% CI [4.101, 4.309].

These results indicate that members have favorable
attitudes toward credit union employees.

# R6: Operational Effectiveness

This research question examines members' perceptions of
the operational effectiveness of the credit union.

## Data Preparation

```{r}
#| include: false

r6_vars <- c(
  "q9", "q10", "q11", "q12",
  "q31", "q32", "q33", "q34", "q37"
)

lapply(r6_vars, function(v) {
  list(
    Question = v,
    Description = attr(efcu[[v]], "label"),
    Labels = attr(efcu[[v]], "labels"),
    Frequency = table(efcu[[v]], useNA = "ifany")
  )
})
```

## Data Recoding

Q37 is reverse-coded so that higher scores represent
more favorable evaluations of operational effectiveness.
No Opinion responses are treated as missing values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-recoding
#| tbl-cap: "Recoding of Overall Operational Effectiveness"

efcu$Q37_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q37 %in% 1:5,
  6 - as.numeric(efcu$q37),
  NA_real_
)

table(
  Original = efcu$q37,
  Recoded = efcu$Q37_r,
  useNA = "ifany"
)
```

Q9 retains its original response categories. Q10 is
reverse-coded so that higher scores indicate better
statement accuracy. Q11 and Q12 are recoded so that
Yes = 2 and No = 1. Undefined responses are treated
as missing values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-valid-responses
#| tbl-cap: "Valid and Missing Responses for Q9-Q12"

efcu$q9_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q9 %in% 1:5,
  as.numeric(efcu$q9),
  NA_real_
)

efcu$q10_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q10 %in% 1:4,
  5 - as.numeric(efcu$q10),
  NA_real_
)

efcu$q11_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q11 %in% 1:2,
  3 - as.numeric(efcu$q11),
  NA_real_
)

efcu$q12_r <- ifelse(
  efcu$q12 %in% 1:2,
  3 - as.numeric(efcu$q12),
  NA_real_
)

r6_chi_vars <- c("q9_r", "q10_r", "q11_r", "q12_r")

r6_valid <- data.frame(
  Question = r6_chi_vars,
  Valid = sapply(efcu[r6_chi_vars],
                 function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
  Missing = sapply(efcu[r6_chi_vars],
                   function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
)

kable(r6_valid, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Descriptive Statistics

Frequency and percentage distributions are used to
summarize members' responses to Q9 through Q12.
Missing responses are excluded from the percentage
calculations.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-frequency
#| tbl-cap: "Frequency and Percentage Distributions for Q9-Q12"

r6_frequency <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r6_chi_vars, function(v) {
  x <- na.omit(efcu[[v]])
  freq <- table(x)

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
    Response = names(freq),
    Frequency = as.numeric(freq),
    Percentage = round(
      as.numeric(prop.table(freq)) * 100, 2
    )
  )
}))

kable(r6_frequency, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Test

Chi-square goodness-of-fit tests are conducted to
determine whether the observed response distributions
differ significantly from equal expected proportions.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-chi-square
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Tests for Q9-Q12"

r6_levels <- list(
  q9_r = 1:5,
  q10_r = 1:4,
  q11_r = 1:2,
  q12_r = 1:2
)

r6_chi_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r6_chi_vars, function(v) {
  x <- na.omit(efcu[[v]])
  freq <- table(factor(x, levels = r6_levels[[v]]))
  test <- chisq.test(freq)

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
    N = length(x),
    Chi_Square = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 3),
    df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
    P_Value = format.pval(test$p.value,
                         digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    Significant = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05,
                         "Yes", "No")
  )
}))

kable(r6_chi_tests, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Descriptive Statistics for Q31-Q34 and Q37

Descriptive statistics are calculated to summarize
members' evaluations of operational effectiveness.
Higher scores represent more favorable evaluations
for positively worded items.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive Statistics for Operational Effectiveness"

r6_rating_vars <- c("q31", "q32", "q33", "q34", "Q37_r")

r6_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r6_rating_vars, function(v) {
  x <- as.numeric(efcu[[v]])
  x <- x[x %in% 1:5]

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(v),
    N = length(x),
    Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
    SD = round(sd(x), 3),
    Minimum = min(x),
    Maximum = max(x)
  )
}))

kable(r6_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

## One-Sample t-test for Operational Effectiveness

One-sample t-tests are conducted to determine whether
the mean ratings for Q31-Q34 and Q37 differ
significantly from the midpoint of 3.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-ttest
#| tbl-cap: "One-Sample t-tests for Operational Effectiveness"

r6_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r6_rating_vars, function(v) {
  x <- as.numeric(efcu[[v]])
  x <- x[x %in% 1:5]

  test <- t.test(x, mu = 3)

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(v),
    N = length(x),
    Mean = round(mean(x), 3),
    SD = round(sd(x), 3),
    t = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 3),
    df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
    P_Value = format.pval(test$p.value,
                         digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    Significant = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05,
                         "Yes", "No")
  )
}))

kable(r6_tests, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Data Visualization

```{r}
#| label: fig-r6-ratings
#| fig-cap: "Mean Ratings of Operational Effectiveness"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(r6_summary, aes(x = Question, y = Mean)) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "steelblue",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 3,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Mean)),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 5),
    breaks = 0:5
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Survey Question",
    y = "Mean Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Findings and Insights

The chi-square goodness-of-fit tests for Q9 through Q12
indicate that all response distributions differ
significantly from equal expected proportions
(p < .001).

The mean ratings for Q31 through Q34 and Q37 range
from 3.461 to 4.066. All five mean ratings are
significantly higher than the midpoint of 3
(p < .001), indicating generally favorable
perceptions of operational effectiveness.

Q37 received the highest mean rating (M = 4.066),
followed by Q31 (M = 3.945). Q34 received the lowest
mean rating (M = 3.461), suggesting that simplifying
loan applications may be an area for improvement.

Overall, members evaluate the credit union's
operations positively, although opportunities
remain to improve operational processes.

# R4a: Employee Proficiency by Member Residence

This research question examines whether attitudes
toward employee proficiencies differ between members
who live in the area of the firm's headquarters and
members who live elsewhere.

## Data Preparation

```{r}
#| include: false

attr(efcu$q38, "label")
attr(efcu$q38, "labels")
table(efcu$q38, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Descriptive Statistics

Descriptive statistics are used to compare attitudes
toward employee proficiencies between members living
in the headquarters area and those living elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Employee Proficiency by Member Residence"

efcu$Residence <- factor(
  efcu$q38,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("Headquarters Area", "Elsewhere")
)

r4a_summary <- efcu |>
  dplyr::group_by(Residence) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = sum(!is.na(Att_Employee)),
    Mean = round(mean(Att_Employee, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD = round(sd(Att_Employee, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(r4a_summary)
```

## Independent Samples t-test

An independent samples t-test is conducted to determine
whether attitudes toward employee proficiencies differ
significantly between members living in the headquarters
area and those living elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a-t-test
#| tbl-cap: "Independent Samples t-test by Member Residence"

r4a_test <- t.test(
  Att_Employee ~ Residence,
  data = efcu,
  var.equal = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  t = round(as.numeric(r4a_test$statistic), 3),
  df = round(as.numeric(r4a_test$parameter), 3),
  P_Value = format.pval(
    r4a_test$p.value,
    digits = 3, eps = 0.001
  ),
  Lower_CI = round(r4a_test$conf.int[1], 3),
  Upper_CI = round(r4a_test$conf.int[2], 3),
  Significant = ifelse(
    r4a_test$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No"
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Data Visualization

```{r}
#| label: fig-r4a-residence
#| fig-cap: "Mean Employee Proficiency Ratings by Member Residence"

ggplot(r4a_summary,
       aes(x = Residence, y = Mean)) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "steelblue",
    width = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 3,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Mean)),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 5),
    breaks = 0:5
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Member Residence",
    y = "Mean Employee Proficiency Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Findings and Insights

Members living in the headquarters area reported a
slightly higher mean employee proficiency rating
(M = 4.281, SD = 0.575) than members living elsewhere
(M = 4.144, SD = 0.606).

However, the independent samples t-test revealed no
statistically significant difference between the two
groups (t = 1.302, p = 0.1955).

These findings suggest that members generally have
positive perceptions of employee proficiencies,
regardless of their residential location. There is
insufficient evidence to conclude that employee
proficiency ratings differ by member residence.

# R4b: Awareness of Services by Member Residence

This research question examines whether awareness of
credit union services differs between members living
in the headquarters area and those living elsewhere.

## Data Preparation

```{r}
#| include: false

r4b_vars <- paste0("q", 13:26)

lapply(r4b_vars, function(v) {
  list(
    Question = v,
    Description = attr(efcu[[v]], "label"),
    Labels = attr(efcu[[v]], "labels"),
    Frequency = table(efcu[[v]], useNA = "ifany")
  )
})
```

## Data Recoding

Q13–Q26 are reverse-coded so that higher scores
represent greater awareness and usage of credit
union services. Responses outside the valid range
are treated as missing values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-recoding
#| tbl-cap: "Valid and Missing Responses for Q13–Q26"

for (v in r4b_vars) {
  x <- as.numeric(efcu[[v]])

  efcu[[paste0(v, "_r")]] <- ifelse(
    x %in% 1:3,
    4 - x,
    NA_real_
  )
}

r4b_recoded <- paste0(r4b_vars, "_r")

r4b_valid <- data.frame(
  Question = toupper(r4b_vars),
  Valid = sapply(efcu[r4b_recoded],
                 function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
  Missing = sapply(efcu[r4b_recoded],
                   function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
)

knitr::kable(r4b_valid, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Two-way Cross-tabulation

Cross-tabulations are used to compare awareness
and usage of credit union services between members
living in the headquarters area and those living
elsewhere. Row percentages are calculated to
compare response distributions across residence groups.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-crosstab
#| tbl-cap: "Service Awareness by Member Residence"

r4b_crosstab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r4b_recoded, function(v) {

  tab <- table(
    Residence = efcu$Residence,
    Awareness = factor(
      efcu[[v]],
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Unaware",
        "Aware but Not Used",
        "Aware and Used"
      )
    )
  )

  pct <- prop.table(tab, margin = 1) * 100

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
    Residence = rownames(tab),
    Unaware = round(pct[, 1], 2),
    Aware_Not_Used = round(pct[, 2], 2),
    Aware_Used = round(pct[, 3], 2)
  )
}))

knitr::kable(r4b_crosstab, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Chi-Square Test of Independence

Chi-square tests of independence are conducted to
determine whether awareness and usage of credit
union services are significantly associated with
member residence.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-chi-square
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-Square Tests of Independence for Q13–Q26"

r4b_chi_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r4b_recoded, function(v) {

  tab <- table(
    efcu$Residence,
    factor(efcu[[v]], levels = 1:3)
  )

  tab <- tab[rowSums(tab) > 0,
             colSums(tab) > 0, drop = FALSE]

  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))

  data.frame(
    Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
    N = sum(tab),
    Chi_Square = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 3),
    df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
    P_Value = format.pval(
      test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001
    ),
    Min_Expected = round(min(test$expected), 2),
    Significant = ifelse(
      test$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No"
    )
  )
}))

knitr::kable(r4b_chi_tests, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Additional Validation: Fisher's Exact Test

Fisher's exact tests are conducted for items with
small expected cell frequencies to validate the
chi-square test results.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-fisher
#| tbl-cap: "Fisher's Exact Tests for Small Expected Frequencies"

r4b_fisher_vars <- c(
  "q15_r", "q18_r", "q19_r",
  "q22_r", "q24_r", "q25_r"
)

r4b_fisher_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  r4b_fisher_vars, function(v) {

    tab <- table(
      efcu$Residence,
      factor(efcu[[v]], levels = 1:3)
    )

    tab <- tab[rowSums(tab) > 0,
               colSums(tab) > 0, drop = FALSE]

    test <- fisher.test(tab)

    data.frame(
      Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
      N = sum(tab),
      P_Value = format.pval(
        test$p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001
      ),
      Significant = ifelse(
        test$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No"
      )
    )
  }
))

knitr::kable(r4b_fisher_tests, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Data Visualization

The following figure compares service awareness
between members living in the headquarters area
and those living elsewhere. Awareness includes
members who have used the service and those who
are aware of the service but have not used it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-r4b-awareness
#| fig-cap: "Service Awareness by Member Residence"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

r4b_plot <- r4b_crosstab |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Awareness = Aware_Not_Used + Aware_Used
  )

ggplot(
  r4b_plot,
  aes(
    x = Question,
    y = Awareness,
    fill = Residence
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("steelblue", "orange")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Survey Question",
    y = "Service Awareness (%)",
    fill = "Member Residence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Findings and Insights

The chi-square tests of independence indicate that
none of the 14 service awareness and usage items
(Q13–Q26) show statistically significant associations
with member residence (all p-values > 0.05).

Fisher's exact tests were also conducted for six
items with small expected cell frequencies.
The results support the same conclusion, with
all p-values greater than 0.05.

Overall, there is insufficient statistical evidence
to conclude that service awareness and usage differ
between members living in the headquarters area
and those living elsewhere.

These findings suggest that the credit union may
consider a consistent service communication and
promotion strategy across both geographic groups,
while continuing to monitor individual service
awareness and usage.

# R4c: Operational Effectiveness by Member Residence

This research question examines whether members'
attitudes toward operational effectiveness differ
between those living in the headquarters area
and those living elsewhere.

## Data Preparation

The recoded variables from R6 and the residence
variable from R4a are used for this analysis.

```{r}
#| include: false

r4c_rating_vars <- c(
  "q9_r", "q10_r",
  "q31", "q32", "q33", "q34",
  "Q37_r"
)

r4c_chi_vars <- c("q11_r", "q12_r")

r4c_vars <- c(
  r4c_rating_vars,
  r4c_chi_vars
)

sapply(efcu[r4c_vars], function(x) {
  sum(!is.na(x))
})

table(efcu$Residence, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Descriptive Statistics

Descriptive statistics are calculated to compare
operational effectiveness ratings between members
living in the headquarters area and those living
elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Operational Effectiveness by Member Residence"

r4c_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  r4c_rating_vars, function(v) {

    data.frame(
      Question = toupper(v),
      Residence = efcu$Residence,
      Score = as.numeric(efcu[[v]])
    ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(Score),
        !is.na(Residence)
      ) |>
      dplyr::group_by(Question, Residence) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        N = dplyr::n(),
        Mean = round(mean(Score), 3),
        SD = round(sd(Score), 3),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  }
))

knitr::kable(r4c_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Independent Samples t-test

Independent samples t-tests are conducted to
determine whether operational effectiveness
ratings differ significantly between members
living in the headquarters area and those
living elsewhere.

Welch's t-test is used without assuming equal
population variances.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-t-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Independent Samples t-tests for Operational Effectiveness"

r4c_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  r4c_rating_vars, function(v) {

    temp <- data.frame(
      Score = as.numeric(efcu[[v]]),
      Residence = efcu$Residence
    )

    test <- t.test(
      Score ~ Residence,
      data = temp,
      var.equal = FALSE
    )

    data.frame(
      Question = toupper(v),
      t = round(as.numeric(test$statistic), 3),
      df = round(as.numeric(test$parameter), 3),
      P_Value = format.pval(
        test$p.value,
        digits = 3,
        eps = 0.001
      ),
      Lower_CI = round(test$conf.int[1], 3),
      Upper_CI = round(test$conf.int[2], 3),
      Significant = ifelse(
        test$p.value < 0.05, "Yes", "No"
      )
    )
  }
))

knitr::kable(r4c_tests, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Two-way Cross-tabulation

Two-way cross-tabulations are used to compare
responses to Q11 and Q12 between members living
in the headquarters area and those living elsewhere.

Row percentages are calculated using valid responses
within each residence group.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-crosstab
#| tbl-cap: "Responses to Q11 and Q12 by Member Residence"

r4c_crosstab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  r4c_chi_vars, function(v) {

    tab <- table(
      Residence = efcu$Residence,
      Response = factor(
        efcu[[v]],
        levels = c(1, 2),
        labels = c("No", "Yes")
      )
    )

    pct <- prop.table(tab, margin = 1) * 100

    data.frame(
      Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
      Residence = rownames(tab),
      N = rowSums(tab),
      No = as.numeric(tab[, 1]),
      Yes = as.numeric(tab[, 2]),
      No_Percentage = round(pct[, 1], 2),
      Yes_Percentage = round(pct[, 2], 2)
    )
  }
))

knitr::kable(r4c_crosstab, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Chi-Square Test of Independence

Chi-square tests of independence are conducted to
determine whether responses to Q11 and Q12 are
significantly associated with member residence.

Fisher's exact test is also conducted when expected
cell frequencies are below five.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-chi-square
#| tbl-cap: "Chi-Square Tests of Independence for Q11 and Q12"

r4c_chi_tests <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  r4c_chi_vars, function(v) {

    tab <- table(
      efcu$Residence,
      factor(efcu[[v]], levels = c(1, 2))
    )

    test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))

    fisher_p <- if (min(test$expected) < 5) {
      fisher.test(tab)$p.value
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }

    final_p <- ifelse(
      is.na(fisher_p), test$p.value, fisher_p
    )

    data.frame(
      Question = toupper(sub("_r$", "", v)),
      N = sum(tab),
      Chi_Square = round(
        as.numeric(test$statistic), 3
      ),
      df = as.numeric(test$parameter),
      P_Value = round(test$p.value, 4),
      Min_Expected = round(min(test$expected), 2),
      Fisher_P = round(fisher_p, 4),
      Significant = ifelse(
        final_p < 0.05, "Yes", "No"
      )
    )
  }
))

knitr::kable(r4c_chi_tests, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Findings and Insights

Most operational effectiveness ratings showed no
significant differences between residence groups.

Q34 was the only significant result before multiple
comparison adjustment (t = -2.280, p = 0.0249).
Members living elsewhere reported a higher mean
rating (M = 3.61) than those living in the
headquarters area (M = 3.28).

Neither Q11 (p = 0.5851) nor Q12 (p = 0.2506)
showed a significant association with residence.

Overall, member residence does not appear to be
a major factor in operational effectiveness.
However, the credit union could further investigate
the loan application experience among headquarters
area members. The Q34 result should be interpreted
cautiously due to multiple comparisons.
